result.title: OP-Print: Tracing Membership Imprints in On-Policy Self-Distillation
result.summary: On-policy distillation has been widely adopted for alleviating the distribution mismatch of off-policy distillation. Self-distillation further removes the need for an external teacher by using the student's own outputs, enhanced with extra context or demonstrations, as supervision. This teacher-free design makes on-policy self-distillation practical, yet its privacy risks remain largely unexplored. In particular, using two coupled views of the same training example may strengthen its memorization. Motivated by this, we present the first study of membership inference attacks against on-policy self-distillation. We investigate both gray-box and black-box threat models and propose a unified attack framework, named OP-Print. OP-Print builds on our finding that the supervision imprint in on-policy self-distillation is sparse and structured, concentrating on uncertainty-sensitive correction sites rather than across the entire rollout. Exploiting this property, we construct attack signals tailored to the two access levels: in the gray-box setting, OP-Print directly aggregates the privileged teacher-student residual correction along the same rollout; in the black-box setting, it measures restart-based output-basin stability as an observable surrogate for the hidden correction process. Across diverse models and distillation schemes, all baseline attacks remain essentially at random guessing even under gray-box access, whereas OP-Print is broadly validated to be effective in both gray-box and black-box settings.

AI.brief_summary: 该文首次研究 on-policy 自蒸馏中的成员推断攻击，提出 OP-Print 框架：基于「监督印记稀疏且集中在不确定性敏感修正位点」的发现，分别设计灰盒下的教师-学生残差聚合信号与黑盒下基于重启的输出盆稳定性信号。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「监督印记稀疏、集中于修正位点」的定位方式可供核查，可能启发 LVR 轨迹蒸馏中的贡献分配与监督落点分析，而「重启后输出稳定性作为隐藏更新过程的代理」或可类比用于探测 latent 状态的稳定性与缓存影响；但原文不涉及视觉或多模态推理。
